test_title: SSC CPO 2022 Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
**Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.**

A. The Taj Mahal is an iconic building. Visiting it is an experience worth remembering forever.

B. Taj Mahal is a iconic building. Visiting it is an experience worth remembering forever.

C. The Taj Mahal is an iconic building. Visiting it is a experience worth remembering forever.

D. A Taj Mahal is a iconic building. Visiting it is an experience worth remembering forever.
solution:
The correct answer is: "**The Taj Mahal is an iconic building. Visiting it is an experience worth remembering forever.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence starts with an article "**The**" before **Taj Mahal**, indicating a specific object.
 
• The use of "**an**" before "**iconic building**" is correct as "**iconic**" starts with a vowel sound.
 
• The sentence structure is correct with the subject "**Visiting it**" and the predicate "is an experience worth remembering forever."

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sentence B** is incorrect because it lacks the definite article "The" before "Taj Mahal," which is necessary for proper noun usage in English. Additionally, there should be "an" before "iconic" instead of "a" because "iconic" begins with a vowel sound. These errors make this option grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Sentence C** correctly uses "The" before "Taj Mahal" and "an" before "iconic building." However, it uses "a" before "experience," which is incorrect. Since "experience" begins with a vowel sound, it should be "an experience." This inconsistency in article usage makes this option incorrect.
 
• **Sentence D** is incorrect because it omits the definite article "The" before "Taj Mahal," and it also uses "a" before "Taj Mahal," which is not grammatically correct.
